scope: Correction limited to DCP-LETT-4217F, DCP-LETT-3240, and DCP-LETT-13865 after primary source reading identified enclosure/transcription distinctions.

record_reviews.source_kind: missing cover letter with complete scholarly enclosure transcription
record_reviews.date_assessment: Header identifies William Allport Leighton and gives [before 21 June 1863]. The surviving enclosure is explicitly dated in its own closing attribution as an extract from Abbé José Francisco Correa da Serra to Sir James Edward Smith, 4 July 1795. The cover's composition/sending date is not established because the cover letter is missing; neither date should be recast as an 1844–46 event.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: The enclosure is not Leighton's or Darwin's prose. It is Leighton's copy of part of Correa da Serra's 1795 letter to Smith, transcribed from P. Smith 1832, 2:210–11. The CD annotation records only the reference 'Life of Sir J. E. Smith.'

scholarly_sections_read.quote: [Enclosure]2 Days ago I was at Lee’s3 with our fellow Lambert,4 &, as many species of Verbascum unknown to me were in blossom, I tried in all of them the phænomenon of their [irritability], with the greatest success in all of them. I remember having spoken to you about it; & as probably the English Verbasca are now in flower about Norwich I will be very glad if you observe it minutely. Strike with a stick & with some force, the stem of the plant under the branches 2 or 3 times & wait patiently for some minutes; you will see the limbus of the corolla move towards the centre, & afterwards the basis of the tubus slowly detach itself from the receptacle & fall—& immedly. the calyx close itself with impatience & embrace the seeds & that will happen to all the open flowers one after another.5 In Portugal6 I had observed it in the Verbascum Thapsi—sinuatum— Blattaria—now at Lee’s in many others & I wish I cod. observe all its species & the Celsiæ:— I know nothing analogous in other plants Next year this will be followed up, & made a Memoir for our Society.7 Abbé Correa to Sir JES. in lit July 4. 1795 see Life of Sir JES. 2.2108
scholarly_sections_read.content_note: This is a substantive historical botanical report and experimental instruction about Verbascum floral irritability, followed by the 1795 attribution. It supplies preserved enclosure prose, but not the missing cover or a Darwin response prompt.

scholarly_sections_read.quote: CD annotationsEnd of letter: ‘Life of Sir J. E. Smith.’ ink
scholarly_sections_read.content_note: The annotation is a later reference note and does not identify when Darwin wrote it or make the enclosure Darwin's own voice.

footnote_constraints: Footnote 2 says the letter with which the enclosure was sent has not been found and identifies the enclosure as a copy from P. Smith 1832.

Footnote 5 says Darwin attempted the Verbascum lychnitis experiment unsuccessfully and cites experimental notes dated 21 June 1863; this is a later Darwin experiment, not the date of the copied 1795 text.
Footnote 7 explains the reference to the Linnean Society and says no Correa da Serra Verbascum paper in its transactions has been found.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The missing cover prevents identification of an incoming prompt or receipt event. The enclosure's 1795 authorship and Leighton's later transmission cannot be used as a Darwin-response pair in 1844–46.
record_reviews.correction: Withdraw the earlier characterization that the record lacked a surviving substantive transcription. Mark only the main cover as unavailable; retain the enclosure as fully transcribed scholarly material with distinct historical authorship and date.

record_reviews.date_assessment: Header gives H. W. Bates [before 25 September 1861]. Footnote 2 says the letter is badly damaged and only occasional words or parts of sentences are legible. This is outside the 1844–46 period and cannot supply a usable prompt.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: The body block is the bracketed catalogue synopsis '[Reports on some of the results of his study of various Amazonian insects.]'; it is not a transcription of Bates's surviving prose. The editorial summary is only 'Mention of Volucella.'
